---
title: "OMK JSON"
---

This page is executable:
every code block below runs when the documentation is built.

`openmusickit.io.omk_json` writes a whole graph as JSON and reads it back.
It is OMK's own format, and it keeps everything:
every node and edge with its id,
every value with all of its fields,
and the metadata applications attach (`meta`, and the graph's `info`).
It holds the music and nothing about the implementation,
so another implementation of OMK, in any language, can read and write the same files.
The format is [specified separately](spec/omk-json.qmd),
with [JSON Schemas](spec/omk-json.qmd#schemas) to check documents against.

```{python}
import json
import tempfile
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import openmusickit as omk
from openmusickit.io.omk_json import dumps, loads, read, write
from openmusickit.io.musicxml import read as read_musicxml
from openmusickit.systems.wsmn.symbols import *
```

## Writing and reading

`dumps` gives a graph's document as text, and `loads` reads one back as a new graph.
Here is one note with a staccato dot.

```{python}
graph = omk.OmkGraph(omk.GraphMeta(name="Sketch"))
note = omk.NoteEvent(tones={C}, duration=quarter)
graph.add_node(note)
graph.add_articulation(omk.Marking(mark=staccato), note)

text = dumps(graph)
print(text[:600])
```

Every node and edge carries its id (`@id`) and its type (`@type`);
types from Western Standard Music Notation are prefixed `wsmn:`,
and the document lists the vocabularies it uses under `vocabularies`.
A value is written in full, even a ready-made one like `staccato`,
so a document never depends on OMK's tables of symbols.

A round trip is exact both ways.
The graph read back holds the same objects, with the same ids,
and writing it again gives the same text, byte for byte:

```{python}
again = loads(text)
print(again.get_node(note.id) == note)
print(dumps(again) == text)
```

The text is *canonical*: keys sorted, nodes and edges sorted by id,
numbers and strings written one way only.
So two graphs holding the same music with the same ids
write the same bytes, whatever order they were built in,
and a change to a score is a small change to its file.

## Files

`write` and `read` do the same with a file, as UTF-8.
`OmkGraph.from_file` and `export_file` dispatch `.json` here by suffix,
as they do `.musicxml` to the MusicXML reader and writer;
`.omk.json` is the suggested suffix.

```{python}
lead_sheet = Path("../tests/scores/second-line-joe-avery/SECOND LINE, (THE ORIGINAL) (JOE AVERY BLUES).xml")
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore", omk.OmkWarning)
    tune = read_musicxml(lead_sheet)

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "second-line.omk.json"
tune.export_file(out)
copy = omk.OmkGraph.from_file(out)

print(f"{out.stat().st_size:,} bytes, {len(list(copy.nodes()))} nodes")
print(copy.is_equivalent(tune))
print({node.id for node in copy.nodes()} == {node.id for node in tune.nodes()})
```

The MusicXML reader's notes for its writer (`meta["musicxml"]`) come through too,
so a score read from MusicXML, saved as JSON and loaded again
writes the same music back to MusicXML.

`OmkGraph.import_json_graph` adds a document's contents to a graph that already has some,
keeping their ids;
it refuses a document holding an id the graph already has, and then adds nothing.

## What is refused

A reader is strict.
A document that breaks the specification is refused with an `OmkJsonError`,
and nothing is added to any graph:
a value outside its domain, a field a type does not have,
two edges where the graph allows one.
Values must be written in their one canonical form:
a half note is `1/2`, never `2/4`.

```{python}
document = json.loads(text)
duration = next(n for n in document["nodes"] if n["@type"] == "NoteEvent")["duration"]
duration.update(numerator=2, denominator=8)
try:
    loads(json.dumps(document))
except omk.errors.OmkJsonError as error:
    print(error)
```

A writer refuses what a reader would reject,
naming the node or edge,
and `meta` must be plain JSON data (no tuples, no `Fraction`s):

```{python}
note.meta["position"] = (120, 40)
try:
    dumps(graph)
except omk.errors.UnexportableError as error:
    print(str(error)[:120], "...")
note.meta["position"] = [120, 40]
```

## Extensions

The types in a document come from *vocabularies*:
`omk` for the core and `wsmn` for Western Standard Music Notation,
which are always available.
An extension of OMK that adds its own node, edge or value types
publishes a vocabulary of its own,
and a program that uses the extension passes it to `dumps`, `loads`, `read` and `write`
(`vocabularies=[...]`).
A document lists every vocabulary it needs;
reading one without them names what is missing:

```{python}
document = json.loads(text)
document["vocabularies"]["chant"] = {"uri": "https://example.org/spec/chant", "version": "0.3"}
try:
    loads(json.dumps(document))
except omk.errors.OmkJsonError as error:
    print(error)
```
